sentences.text: Amazonsaurus maranhensis is the only known species within the dinosaur genus Amazonsaurus.
This animal was a large, four-legged herbivore characterized by a long neck and a whiplash-style tail.
Estimates of its size vary, with Elver Luiz Mayer suggesting a length of around 10 meters, while Gregory S. Paul proposed it reached 12 meters.
In contrast, Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 that the dinosaur weighed 5000 kg.
The dorsal vertebrae featured slightly opisthocoelous centra that were wide and low, with a flat bottom giving them a squared shape.
Deep pleurocoels, which held air sacs, occupied most of the internal space on the sides of these dorsal vertebrae.
Unlike other rebbachisaurids, the neural spines on the tail vertebrae were straight, inclined backward, and oriented at a 45-degree angle from the middle of the vertebra body.
The neural arches of the tail vertebrae were extremely tall, a trait typical of diplodocoids.
The chevrons were L-shaped with open haemal canals and a posterior distal process, differing from those of Limaysaurus.
Amazonsaurus fossils were first found in the Mata locality in the Brazilian Amazon.
This discovery was the first of dinosaur fossils in the Amazon Basin and the first record of a sauropod from the Lower Cretaceous of Brazil.
Ismar de Souza Carvalho, Leonardo dos Santos Avilla, and Leonardo Salgado formally named the genus and species in 2003.
Amazonsaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
The animal belongs to the family Rebbachisauridae, with Rebbachisauridae serving as its parent group.
Amazonsaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous Period.
It lived between 125 and 100 million years ago during the Aptian and Albian epochs.
The time range for Amazonsaurus is from the Aptian to the Albian, between 119.57 and 106.3 million years ago.
Amazonsaurus lived in floodplain deposits near a river delta.

There is a debate regarding the precise classification of Amazonsaurus; while it belongs to the family Rebbachisauridae and its parent group is Rebbachisauridae, high dorsal spines identify it as a diplodocoid sauropod, and one analysis places it as more derived than rebbachisaurids but more basal than dicraeosaurids and diplodocids within Diplodocoidea.
